analysis: Examined base_text of ClusterService.swift lines 911-1536 (status(), checkForUpdate, checkApproval, lastError/servingNotice log reads, publish/supervision acknowledgement, supervise part start/stop, partEnvironment, removeEndedApproval, leaderAPIPort, stopChild). Per the range map, the changed head ranges are 99, 144-147, 164-175 and 337-420, all outside these base units. The visible patch makes `responder` internal instead of private and renames the cable-check timers to responderCheck/controlCheck. It also adds a `listening: Listening` init parameter for the cable listeners' port and pairing checks (listenerChange). Nothing in these units changes. Approval lifetime enforcement is unchanged: supervise stops parts whose approval ended (1331-1337) and removeEndedApproval saves the setup without the approval (1387-1393, 1468-1483). Worker digest pin re-planning (964-1013), the command lock and log/status file handling are also unchanged. Status files are written atomically in the owner's service directory and the rank log is created 0600. Cache reclaim at 1365-1369 is untouched and is only loosely related to T-041. No regression is identifiable in these units. Integration questions: confirm what the new Listening/listenerChange code (head 337-420) does on a pairing change. Check whether it reopens or replaces the responder link listener without re-checking pairing/peer identity. Check whether widening `responder` to internal exposes it to other module code that could swap listeners. These are local cluster-link trust questions not covered by a canonical TB; the threat model may need a cluster-link boundary if the listener accepts peer commands such as status or approval sync, the latter sent via live.command at 1108. The head source is not in this batch.
